legend.component: the shape tells the node kind (the alias lines give the kind); solid arrow = runtime relation, dashed arrow = static relation; arrow label = relation name; the number labels of component-overview = count of connections between buildings (not a weight or a latency)
legend.class: each box is a class, an interface or an enumeration; <<...>> names the kind; member lines are methods or enumeration values; arrows = use or association
legend.state: each box is a state name; [*] points at the initial state and an arrow to [*] marks a terminal state; arrow label = guard and error code
legend.er: each box is a table; a column line = type name key (PK primary, FK foreign, UK unique); the symbols at the ends of a relation line = cardinality; unspecified = no cardinality written, drawn as the weakest claim zero-or-more
legend.sequence: each arrow is one event of the trace (the first 60 at most); solid arrow = call or message, dashed arrow = return, an arrow with a cross = a failed result; arrow label = event type and result; the participant aliases are in the alias lines
legend.staterun: only the 6 nodes with the most state changes are drawn; each box is one state of one node; arrow label _N = trace index N, which is event number N+1

start.lead: This is the entry card of the reading surface: read it first, then pick pages with the table below. Do not read `index.html`, `docs/` or `prompts/` as a whole. `<dist>` is the absolute path of the directory this page is in; keep it in the `grep` and `sed` recipes.
start.identity: Project `{project}` · language {language} · model stamp m={stamp} · mode {mode} · content: {content}
route: | Where an id is and what it is | `gemarc_atlas_index scope="ids:<id>"`; without tools: `grep -P '^<id>\t' <dist>/ids.tsv` | page and line of the reply; context: `sed -n '1,9p;<hdr>,+2p;<line>p' <dist>/<path>` |
| What a node is connected to (outgoing and inbound) | find its home page as above | the 'Outgoing connections' and 'Inbound connections' tables of the home page, one page for both |
| Who cites requirement, evidence or test X | `grep -P '^X\t' <dist>/refs.tsv` | path and line of the reply |
| How a requirement is realised | {r} | the table of elements that implement it; read their structure pages for their connections |
| Data tables, state machines, space | {d}; {m}; {w} | same |
| What a case expects and gives | {c} | the case block; a result block exists only for sealed cases or cases the user approved, the others say not sealed |
| What an intervention changes | {v} | the intervention block and its comparisons; each comparison has ledger, verdict and basis, unsealed ones say so |
| Quality, withheld items, exclusion table | {q} | same |
| Terms, markers, grade words | {g} | the grade ruler is inline in the reading line of every page |
start.route_ui: | Check a frontend implementation | {ui} | the screen card, then the PNG, the SVG only for exact marks |

reason.T: no open item, constraint or policy
reason.D: no data-table node or data policy

stale: With gemarc tools: `gemarc_atlas_index scope="stamp"`, one line `built=<8hex> current=<8hex> stale=<true|false>`; `gemarc_atlas_status view=next` also always has an entry or staleness line.
Files only (a pack that was sent to you): the pages are a snapshot and cannot be checked online; report the `m=` of the page head to the sender.
The `m=` of line 2 differs from this page: two builds were mixed, discard all of it.
skip: `index.html`{size}: the single-page viewer for a browser, not the reading surface.
`docs/<language>/{REQ,BD,DD}.md`{size_docs}, `prompts/*.md`, `oracle-sheet.md`: hand-over material, a whole read is cut short.
`ids.tsv`, `refs.tsv`, `manifest.jsonl`: look things up with `grep` or `index`, never read them whole.
`site/` (when present): the HTML twin of each Markdown page, for a browser and for WebFetch, not for a shell (`cat`); the text is the same as the Markdown page, an AI reads the Markdown by default.
start.ui_warn: warning: declared as no screens, but the model has screen clues; the final report must repeat this line word for word.
start.client: Claude Code Read allows 256 KB and 25k tokens per file and Grep hides lines above 500 characters; Codex uses a shell and `cat` keeps the head and the tail of a long output and drops the middle; Hermes read_file allows 2,000 characters a line. When the output shows `truncated` or `omitted`, or the total line count in the page head is larger than the lines you see, re-read in parts with `sed -n 'a,bp'`; a visible sentinel line does not prove a whole read.
start.client_ref: The read limits and the truncation hints of each client are in §G01.
start.results: 4D/5D result pages (the run results of cases and interventions) are files: read them with Read, never through `gemarc_atlas_doc`. Only sealed items or items the user approved have a result, the others say 'not sealed'; every result carries its ledger, its scope and its nature (derived inside the model, not measured).
start.cannot: Isolated nodes, nodes without a requirement: the model does not tell 'not written' from 'none' (`[N/A]` means both), so this surface cannot answer; to answer, make it an explicit `[NONE-DECLARED]` in the model first.
start.covers: entry, route table, directory of dimensions
start.howto: route by section 2; do not read big files whole

h: A read that is cut short
How to read a result block
page: A page id is written `§S07`; `§` is not in the first-character set of any model id, so `§S07` is never an id of the model. Page ids and line numbers hold only inside one model stamp `m=`.
A reference line is `id` (a name of at most 24 characters, longer: cut and `name…`) + kind + home page `§page id`; link texts always contain an id or a page id.
glossary.ruler: Grades high to low: {ruler}. A grade word only says how well a fact is supported.
marks: `[N/A]`: none (not written or not applicable; the model does not tell the two apart).
`[NONE-DECLARED]`, `[NONE-IN-SCOPE]`: an explicit empty state, not an omission.
ids: An id is an opaque string, never split at `:`. Edge ids often contain both end node ids but alias edges do not: the edges of a node are the rows of the outgoing and inbound tables of its home page, not what `grep` finds.
A file name is only a page id or an encoded id and carries no meaning; trust `manifest.jsonl` and `ids.tsv`.
Look an id up exactly with the anchored `grep -P '^<id>\t' <dist>/ids.tsv`; `grep -F` matches substrings and finds too much.
fold: `see note [k]`: a table cell that was too long; its full text is on the `[k]` line under the table.
A line that starts with `(cont.)` continues the line before.
A unit longer than one page is continued: every part repeats the identity lines and the table header, the heading says `(rows of this part / all rows, rows a-b)`, the foot names the next part.
trunc: When the output shows `truncated` or `omitted`, or the total line count in the page head is larger than the lines you see, re-read in parts with `sed -n 'a,bp'`; a visible sentinel line does not prove a whole read.

Claude Code Read allows 256 KB and 25k tokens per file and Grep hides lines above 500 characters; Codex `cat` keeps the head and the tail of a long output; Hermes read_file allows 2,000 characters a line.
cannot: Which nodes have no requirement and which are isolated: not answerable, `[N/A]` does not tell 'not written' from 'none'.

The run results of cases and interventions: only in the result blocks of sealed items or items the user approved, and their nature is derived inside the model (not measured); an item that is not sealed has no result and none can be inferred from another page.
glossary.covers: terms, markers and the grade ruler
glossary.howto: look words up as needed, no need to read it through
results: Ledger: the first word `sealed` = an expectation the AI wrote and sealed before any result existed; the second word = the user approved the expectation. An item without a ledger line has no result.

The verdict words are only `pass`, `fail` and `undecided`. `asserts k of n nodes`: n is the number of nodes in the model, k the number of nodes the author listed in the expectation; a verdict compares only those k, the other n-k are not asserted.

'Unlisted' means the opposite in the two columns: in the author's expectation an unlisted node is not asserted; in the engine terminal state an unlisted node is Idle (the engine records only nodes that are not Idle).

The nature is always `derived inside the model (not measured)`: the result follows from the rules of the model itself, it is not a measurement of a real system. The weakest grade is the weakest link of the basis; a basis written `none (reason)` is no basis.

docs.title: Hand-over material
lines: The files here are hand-over material for people and downstream steps, not the reading surface of an AI; an AI reads `START.md` one level up first.
`docs/<language>/REQ.md`, `BD.md`, `DD.md`: three formal documents, each one more detailed than the one before{sizes}; a whole read is cut short.

The documents are derived mechanically from the same model and every statement comes from an authored fact; the DD connection table has a label column and the evidence table a repository alias and a line range column.
